clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: Delphine stopped cooking and went to her daughter Odette's every evening, Duncan took night shifts and distanced from Odette, Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work, Celeste separated from Anton in August, Odette lay awake over her mother and Anton, and Callum had ear infections through the winter. These shifts spread across the extended family in the months after the death; Delphine's move to a job at the library in May 1979 is where the acute distress settles.

clusters.name: Odette's bedrest in pregnancy, 1984–1985
clusters.reason: Around Odette ordered to bed in March 1984: Hazel came every morning to keep the house, argued with Duncan over how she kept it, Callum stammered again after a year free of it, and you felt anxious at bedtime. Three shifts that count sit close in these months, with Hazel's overfunctioning and the conflict between her and Duncan touching Callum and you at the same time.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1997
clusters.reason: Hazel was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in September 1986; within the following decade, Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments, Duncan phoned his father nightly for news of her, argued with Lyle over who should help their parents, Ambrose developed chest pains, Duncan drank most evenings, and he and Odette fought over his evenings at his parents' house. These shifts in Duncan and Ambrose pile up through the years as Hazel's illness deepened; the period settles in June 1997 when she moved into the nursing home.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home for the north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Callum left home in May 1999 for a job at the mines up north; in the months around this: he and Duncan argued most nights over his plans, Odette could not settle at the thought of him so far away, Duncan missed days at work and sat up late in the garage, Ines skipped school through the autumn, Odette took Ines with her everywhere, and by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and had passed her exams. The shifts across Duncan, Odette and Ines cluster in these months; Ines's return to school marks where the acute upset settles.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Hazel died in January 2003; within the following months, you could not sleep more than a few hours a night, stopped going to the bookshop and were let go in May, dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark, and by November you had taken a job at the garden centre and were sleeping through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
